fact_text: Interest coverage divides EBIT (operating profit) by interest expense, showing whether core operating profit can cover the cost of borrowing.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: OGDC's interest coverage is about 49 times: operating profit of about 285 billion against interest expense of about 5.8 billion. The presenter said 49%, but the figures give a multiple.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: Inventory turnover divides cost of goods sold by average inventory; for oil and gas firms, gas is usually left out of inventory because it is distributed as it is produced.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: OGDC's inventory turnover is about 5.6 times: cost of goods sold of about 169 billion against average inventory of about 30 billion.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: Dividing 365 days by the 5.6 turnover gives an inventory cycle of about 65 days, so crude oil and LPG sit in storage roughly two months before they are sold.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: The presenter says many companies hold inventory far longer than OGDC, tying up capital, so OGDC's shorter inventory cycle is a positive.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: Asset turnover divides net sales by average total assets, showing how much revenue the company generates for each unit of assets it holds.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: OGDC's asset turnover is about 24%, from net sales of about 401 billion in 2025 against average total assets of about 1,654 billion.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: Current ratio divides current assets by current liabilities, testing whether short-term assets can cover obligations due within the year.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: OGDC's current ratio is about 8.9 times, with current assets of about 1,123 billion against current liabilities of about 125 billion.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: The presenter calls OGDC essentially cash-rich, implying it can meet short-term obligations and that the risk of default on them is very low.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: Effective tax rate is total tax paid divided by profit before tax, showing the overall share of profits taken by tax.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: OGDC's effective tax rate for 2025 is about 39%, with profit before tax of about 279 billion and tax paid of about 109 billion.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: Quick ratio subtracts inventory from current assets before dividing by current liabilities; it is stricter because inventory cannot be turned into cash quickly.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: OGDC's inventory is only about 30 billion, so excluding it barely changes its liquidity picture compared with the current ratio.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: Many analysts deduct circular debt from receivables when judging liquidity; the presenter keeps it included in OGDC's calculation rather than deducting it.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)

fact_text: OGDC's net interest income of about 231 billion equals about 14% of its total assets of about 1,654 billion.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Liquidity Ratios Explained | Part 08 | Stock Analysis using SCSTrade.com | Fundamental Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-03-30)
